newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees more corn exports, little market impact.
newsitem.headline: China sees more corn exports, little market impact.

text.p: China could export 200,000-300,000 tonnes of corn in the near future, officials said on Monday, but ruled out what they called large-scale overseas sales that could hit international prices.

An official of the grain bureau in the northeastern corn-producing province of Jilin said officials were considering boosting exports of corn, and said the amount could be around 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
He declined to give the destination of exports or to specify when the exports would take place.
China would export corn after meeting domestic demand, an official with the Agriculture Ministry in Beijing said.
"Large-scale exports are not possible in the near future," he said, adding that by large-scale he meant exports of a size that could hit international prices.
An official of the State Grain Reserve Administration said he understood that authorities were currently studying the possibility of resuming exports, but declined to give further details.
